thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: *Perf Canary Alert (nightly baseline)* severity=SEV3 (internal)
Signal: `baseline_nightly_drift` (warn-only gate)
Model/shape: `llama3-70b-instruct` / `shape=longctx_streaming_concurrency_ramp`
Region/HW: `us-east-1` / `a100-80gb`
Metric: `TTFT p95` +63% vs baseline (threshold 15%)
Run: `perf-canary #11872` artifact: https://console.redwood.example/perf/runs/11872
Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/perf-baselines/run?run=11872
Commit: runtime `8f2c9d1` / harness `benchmark-lab 3a0c2e7`
Owner hint: @eng-sre @eng-runtime

Sahana Iyer: seeing the ping. this is from the 02:00 UTC scheduled job. looked clean at first glance but tail is *bad* (p99 also +70%). :eyes:

Sean Gallagher: ack. triaging now. can someone from runtime sanity check if `8f2c9d1` has any scheduler/kernels changes that could explain TTFT only on longctx streaming?

Noah Patel: i don’t think so. `8f2c9d1` was a metadata stamp + no-op config load plumbing (shouldn’t move perf). also weird it’s only one region.

Aisha Bello: dashboards show only `us-east-1` failing, `us-west-2` and `eu-central-1` are within noise. that points to env/fleet.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1. fleet in east had some driver rollout last night (i saw a canary ticket). i’ll check if baseline runner nodes were mixed.

Kira Volkov: can you paste the runner environment metadata from the artifact? the JSON should include driver/CUDA if present.

Sahana Iyer: from the run metadata panel:
- `cuda=12.2`
- `runtime_build=8f2c9d1`
- `driver_version=535.104.05` (BUT there’s also a note: `node_pool=shared-a100-east`)
we don’t currently enforce a single driver, we just record what the first node reports.

Sean Gallagher: that’s a red flag. if the pool is mixed we might be running shards on different drivers.

Hiro Tanaka: if driver differs, kernel selection/autotune behavior can differ (esp flash-attn variants). could easily show up in TTFT for long prefill.

Vanessa Ortiz: confirmed: east shared A100 pool is currently *mixed* during rollout.
Some nodes are still on `525.85.12` due to a drained capacity shortage.

Sean Gallagher: ok. let’s prove it. can someone run `nvidia-smi` on 2-3 of the nodes used by the job? (or check runner logs for node IDs)

Sahana Iyer: runner log has node list:
```
[runner] allocated nodes: ip-10-4-12-88, ip-10-4-19-31, ip-10-4-27-203, ip-10-4-33-9
```
I can exec into one.

Sahana Iyer: on ip-10-4-19-31:
```
$ nvidia-smi
NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12    CUDA Version: 12.0
...
```
On ip-10-4-12-88:
```
$ nvidia-smi
NVIDIA-SMI 535.104.05   Driver Version: 535.104.05   CUDA Version: 12.2
...
```
so yeah, mixed.

Sean Gallagher: that explains it. the run metadata is lying by omission (records one node). we should classify this as env drift, not a real perf regression.

Logan Wright: telemetry side looks ok (TTFT computed server-side). nothing suspicious in metric pipeline. agree env mismatch.

Connor O'Brien: do we need to pause the release train gate? this was posted as “severe regression” and could spook people.

Sean Gallagher: it’s warn-only right now, but we should:
1) annotate the run as invalid (env drift)
2) rerun baseline for `us-east-1` once pinned
3) add a preflight check so we fail fast instead of alerting on bad data

Vanessa Ortiz: immediate mitigation: i can label the `525.*` nodes as `driver_outdated=true` and exclude them from benchmark jobs. longer term we should not run baselines on shared pools mid-rollout.

Sahana Iyer: i can hotfix perf-canary job config to require `nodeSelector: driver=535.104.05` (or whatever label vanessa has). will kick a rerun.

Hiro Tanaka: pls also capture this in the incident notes. for kernels team this is the exact scenario where autotune jitter happens and makes diffs meaningless.

Kira Volkov: action item for tooling: runner should collect per-worker env + assert homogeneity.
Something like:
- collect `driver_version`, `cuda_version`, `gpu_name`, `sm`, `clock_caps`
- if >1 unique value in run => `env_drift` and mark run invalid + suppress baseline comparison

Sean Gallagher: yep. also update paging policy: only page if `env_lock=true` and drift checks pass.

Vanessa Ortiz: quick note: the `525.*` nodes are from the “burst” pool we temporarily borrowed. should be drained in ~6 hours.

Sahana Iyer: rerun started with selector `driver=535.104.05` only. run id `#11879`.

Incident Bot: Update: perf-canary rerun started by @Sahana Iyer
Run: https://console.redwood.example/perf/runs/11879

Sahana Iyer: rerun results are back. TTFT p95 now within +2.8% of baseline, p99 +4% (within variance). throughput also matches.

Sean Gallagher: closing as *false positive due to fleet driver mismatch*. :thumbsup:
Mitigations completed:
- [x] rerun with driver-pinned nodes (run #11879)
- [x] exclude outdated-driver nodes from benchmark jobs (vanessa)
Follow-ups (create tickets):
- preflight env homogeneity check in runner (per-node `nvidia-smi` + CUDA) + mark run invalid if mixed
- perf-canary alert suppression when `env_drift`
- dashboard: surface per-node driver versions in run details

Connor O'Brien: thanks. pls link the follow-up ticket(s) here once created so release notes / gating comms can mention “env drift detection added”.

Vanessa Ortiz: I’ll open an internal ticket for fleet enforcement. name: “benchmark fleet env drift guardrails (driver/CUDA)” and add labels so it routes to me + SRE.

Kira Volkov: i’ll take the runner-side change. will open a perf-canary/benchmark-lab issue and cc @Sahana Iyer.

Sean Gallagher: final note: this is exactly why we need environment pinning before making gates blocking. good catch everyone.
